merged.reason: This is the Erdős–Turán conjecture on additive bases. It needs a lower bound on the maximum of the representation function for every basis of order 2, and no known method rules out a bounded representation function. Best known: Dirac showed r(n) cannot be eventually constant, and Erdős–Fuchs showed the average cannot be nearly constant. The conjecture itself is fully open (erdosproblems.com/28 has 0 proof claims; Tao noted on 5 Apr 2026 that at least one of #28 and #749 holds). merged.reason: As formalized, |h(N) - sqrt N| = O(N^eps) has two halves, and both are open. The upper half needs to beat the N^{1/4} barrier of every known counting method. The lower half, h(N) >= sqrt N - O(N^eps) for all N, needs Singer-type moduli (primes near sqrt N) with gaps N^eps, which is beyond Baker–Harman–Pintz. Best known: h(N) <= sqrt N + 0.98183 N^{1/4} + O(1) (Carter–Hunter–O'Bryant 2025) and the unrefereed Hou–Zhao arXiv:2607.01169 with 0.9435. A forum post (johnakwei, 5 Oct 2026) proves that the Hou–Zhao smoothing framework cannot go below 2sqrt2/3 and cannot improve the exponent 1/4. The only 'proof claims' in the thread are constant improvements, not solutions.

merged.reason: A covering needs exact control of how residue classes with distinct odd moduli overlap. Every known method (the distortion method, sieve products) only gives necessary conditions, and current constructions do not come close to producing an odd covering. Best known results: no odd squarefree covering exists (BBMST 2022). Any odd covering has lcm divisible by 45 and minimum modulus at most 9 (Dai-Li-Li-Yi, arXiv:2611.15110, Nov 2026). The lcm exceeds 10000 (kernel-checked, Mian-Siddique, arXiv:2607.25628) and, by an unverified preprint, exceeds 11,486,475. The Lean statement is faithful: StrictCoveringSystem Z requires distinct ideal moduli, and 'not <= span{2}' means the modulus is odd.

merged.reason: Deciding whether the singular distribution function F of phi(n)/n has a positive finite derivative at some point needs fine multi-scale control of how F's mass sits near badly approximable points. No known technique gives this. Best known: F is continuous and purely singular (Erdős; Schoenberg for existence). There is no 2025-2026 work and the forum thread is empty (0 comments, 0 claims). I checked the Lean statement for gaps: the quantifier ranges over all f with the density property on [0,1], which is not vacuous since Schoenberg gives one. HasDerivWithinAt on Icc 0 1 only sees values on [0,1]. At x=0 the derivative is 0, since the density of phi(n)/n < c decays doubly exponentially. At x=1 there is no finite derivative, since 1-F(1-eps) is about 1/log(1/eps). So the endpoints do not settle the statement, and there is no junk-value gap.

merged.reason: Proving existence in ZFC would need a transfinite Folkman-type construction, a K4-free graph G such that every coloring of its edges with omega colors has a monochromatic triangle. Only the finite version (Folkman 1970, Nesetril-Rodl 1975) and consistency are known: Shelah 1987 ('Consistency of positive partition theorems for graphs and models') shows such a graph exists consistently. That is why the database state is 'not disprovable', defined in the teorth CONTRIBUTING.md as 'open in general, but there exist models where the result is true'. Nobody has shown that it is consistent for no such graph to exist, so a ZFC proof is not ruled out, but none is known. This agrees with the earlier audit. merged.reason: Proving ex(n;G) ~ c n^alpha for every bipartite G needs exact asymptotics, and even the order of growth is unknown for most bipartite graphs, for example C_8, K_{4,4} and the cube Q_3. The Erdos-Simonovits conjecture is open. Asymptotics with a constant are known only in special families: trees (by superadditivity and Fekete), C_4, K_{3,3}, and some K_{s,t} with t large compared with s, where only the order is known. Füredi-Gerbner 2021 show the hypergraph analogue is false for uniformity >= 5. No formalization gap: G may have isolated vertices, the condition of at least 2 edges excludes degenerate cases, and alpha must lie in [1,2). Side remark: for disconnected forests, existence of lim ex(n,F)/n is not given by superadditivity either, so even alpha=1 is not trivial in general.

merged.reason: Proving every realized exponent rational needs control over all bipartite G whose extremal number has the form c n^alpha. No structural theory of that kind exists, and refuting the statement would need an explicit G with an irrational exponent and exact asymptotics, also unknown. Best known goes the other way: Bukh-Conlon 2018 realize every rational in [1,2) as the exponent of a finite family of graphs, and later work (Jiang-Qiu, Conlon-Janzer-Lee and others) realizes many rationals with single graphs, but none of this constrains irrational exponents. The statement is not vacuous: C_4 has ex ~ n^{3/2}/2, so the hypothesis does hold for some G.
